data.value: When Pia attends a meeting, group the transcript into separate bubbles per speaker. Requires a one-time download of a small speaker-recognition model. Changes apply to the next meeting you join.

data.name: Settings_Diarization_SmartAuto_Description
data.value: Pia re-evaluates all voices as the meeting progresses and automatically corrects earlier speaker assignments. Manual tuning is hidden while this is on.

data.value: Hide speaker labels in the transcript

data.name: Settings_Diarization_SuppressLabels_Description
data.value: Shows and exports the transcript without any speaker labels. Bubbles stay grouped and coloured by voice; only the labels, which are the part that claims an identity, are removed. Use this when attribution is visibly wrong — an unlabelled transcript serves a summary better than a confidently mislabelled one.

data.name: Settings_Diarization_MicEchoCancellation
data.value: Cancel speaker echo on the microphone

data.name: Settings_Diarization_MicEchoCancellation_Description
data.value: Routes the microphone through the Windows echo canceller so the other side, coming out of your loudspeakers, is removed before it is transcribed. Without it their words are recorded a second time as yours. Switch it off only if you always wear a headset and dislike the noise suppression and gain control that come with it.

data.name: Settings_Diarization_Threshold_Description
data.value: Tunes how similar two voices must sound to be treated as the same speaker. Higher values split speakers more readily (fewer voices merged); lower values group more voices together.

data.name: Settings_Diarization_MaxSpeakers_Description
data.value: Caps how many distinct speakers Pia creates in one meeting. Set it to the number of participants so one person is not split into several voices. 'No limit' lets Pia detect as many speakers as it hears. Changes apply to the next meeting you join.

data.name: Settings_Diarization_MinSpeech_Description
data.value: How much uninterrupted speech is needed before Pia identifies a speaker. Longer values give more reliable matching and fewer accidental extra speakers, but very short remarks may stay unlabeled. Changes apply to the next meeting you join.

data.name: Settings_MeetingBrowser_Description
data.value: Which browser Pia drives to join meetings. Bundled Chromium is downloaded once and is the most reliable choice. System Chrome and System Edge reuse an installed browser but may be affected by browser updates or enterprise policy; if the chosen browser is unavailable, Pia falls back to bundled Chromium. Use system default detects your default browser and uses it when it is Chrome or Edge, otherwise falls back to bundled.

data.name: Settings_MeetingBrowser_ShowWindow_Description
data.value: When off (default), the browser joins hidden and the meeting plays silently. When on, the browser window is shown on screen and the meeting is audible.

data.name: Settings_ToolPermissions_Page_Description
data.value: Pia asks before a tool changes anything. Three answers on that card skip the next prompt: "Allow once" covers a single call, "Allow this session" lasts until Pia closes, and "Always allow" is kept in your settings and listed below. An "Always allow" grant also applies where nobody can be asked — voice mode, scheduled jobs and agent runs all use it. Agent autonomy is a fourth source: while it is on, agent runs and voice mode skip the prompt for Pia's own write tools.

data.name: Settings_ToolPermissions_Autonomy_Covers
data.value: Covered classes: notes and memory, todos, reminders, scheduled jobs, files.

data.name: Settings_ToolPermissions_Session_Description
data.value: Tools you allowed for this session. Nothing here is saved — all of it disappears when Pia restarts. Forget one to be asked again on the next call.

data.name: Settings_ToolPermissions_Description
data.value: Tools you have granted standing approval to run without confirmation. Revoke a grant to be prompted again on the next call.

data.name: ToolPermissions_Empty
data.value: No tools are always allowed. When you choose "Always allow" on a tool, it appears here.

data.name: Settings_ToolPermissions_Catalog_Description
data.value: Approve a tool here and Pia stops asking for it, exactly as if you had chosen the same answer on a card. Every tool can be allowed for this session or permanently; tick one and the row tells you what that tool can then do unsupervised.

data.name: ToolCatalog_Caution_Destructive
data.value: Worth knowing: this tool destroys data, and an approval here covers later calls whose arguments you never see. Leave it unticked to be asked each time.

data.name: ToolCatalog_Caution_WorkDiscarding
data.value: Worth knowing: this tool can throw away uncommitted work, and an approval here covers later calls whose arguments you never see.

data.name: ToolCatalog_Caution_AuthorityAuthoring
data.value: Worth knowing: this tool sets up work that later runs unattended — approving it once lets Pia widen what it may do without asking again.

data.name: ToolCatalog_Caution_Routine_Destructive
data.value: Worth knowing: this tool destroys data, and a routine runs with nobody watching. Left unticked, a run that reaches for it is refused rather than paused for you.

data.name: ToolCatalog_Caution_Routine_WorkDiscarding
data.value: Worth knowing: this tool can throw away uncommitted work, and a routine runs with nobody watching.

data.name: ToolCatalog_Caution_Routine_AuthorityAuthoring
data.value: Worth knowing: this tool grants permissions later runs will use, so allowing it lets this routine widen what Pia may do.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_NewsBriefing_Query
data.value: Search the web for the main news of the past day about {focus}. At most six headlines, one sentence each, with a source link and a date. Lead with what changed, not with who commented on it, and leave out opinion pieces and yesterday’s news retold. If nothing material happened, say so in one line.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_WordOfTheDay_Query
data.value: Teach one word or phrase in {language}: the word, its pronunciation in plain letters, what it literally means, and three everyday example sentences with translations. Pick something a learner would actually say in conversation. Let today’s date decide which area of life it comes from.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_TopicDigest_Query
data.value: Search the web for what is new on {topic} in the past day. At most five items, one sentence each, with a source link and a date. Only material developments — releases, announcements, results, reversals — never speculation or a retelling of old coverage. If nothing happened, say so in one line.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_SecurityAdvisories_Query
data.value: Search the web for security advisories and patches published in the past day for {products}. One line each: product and version, what the flaw allows, whether a fix or a workaround exists, and the CVE. Anything already being exploited comes first. At most six, from the vendor’s own advisory.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_MarketSnapshot_Query
data.value: Search the web for where these markets stand: {markets}. One line each: the level, the move on the day in percent, and the time the figure is quoted for; if a market is shut, quote its last close and say so. Then at most three lines on what moved them. No forecast and no recommendation.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_StockWatchlist_Query
data.value: Search the web for where these holdings stand: {holdings}. One line each: the last price, the move on the day in percent, and the time the figure is quoted for; if the market is shut, quote the last close and say so. Then at most three lines on what moved them. No forecast, no recommendation.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_SportsRoundup_Query
data.value: Search the web for the past week’s results and the coming week’s fixtures for {teams}. One line per result with the score and the competition, one line per fixture with its date and kick-off time, each with a source link. Add at most two lines on an injury, a transfer or a new manager.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_ClientWatch_Query
data.value: Search the web for what changed in the past week at {accounts} that could affect working with them: funding, results, leadership, acquisitions, a large win or a large loss. At most two items each, one sentence each, with a source link and a date. Close with up to three things to raise next time.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_CompetitorWatch_Query
data.value: Search the web for material developments in the past week at {companies}: launches, pricing changes, funding, leadership changes, outages, withdrawals. At most two items per company, one sentence each, with a source link and a date. A company with nothing material gets its own one-line entry.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_IndustryPulse_Query
data.value: Search the web for what moved in {industry} over the past week. At most six items; for each, one line on what happened, one on why it matters, and one on what to watch next, with a source link and a date. Cover the sector rather than one company, and prefer results and deals over commentary.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_RegulationWatch_Query
data.value: Search the web for regulatory changes published in the past week covering {scope}. For each one: the instrument, the body that issued it, the date it was published, the date it takes effect, and a link to the official text. Then one line on why it matters. At most five. This is not legal advice.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_ReleaseWatch_Query
data.value: Search the web for new releases of {projects} in the past week. One line each: the project, the version, the release date, and the one change most likely to matter to somebody already using it, with a link to the release notes. Mark security fixes and breaking changes. At most six.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_MealIdeas_Query
data.value: Plan the coming week’s dinners around this: {preferences}. Five ideas, one line each, with the dish, roughly how long it takes and its main ingredients. Vary the protein and the cuisine. End with one combined shopping list grouped by aisle, and nothing after it. No calorie counts.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_LearnOneThing_Query
data.value: Explain one idea from {subject} in plain language: the idea in a sentence, how it works in at most five short paragraphs, one worked example, and one common misunderstanding of it. Pick something a curious beginner meets early. Let this week’s date decide which branch it comes from.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_MorningBrief_Query
data.value: Call query_todos with filter pending and query_reminders with filter active, then report today and nothing else: every todo due today, everything marked OVERDUE, and every reminder firing today. One line each with its time, ordered by time of day. No advice and no encouragement.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_MeetingFollowup_Query
data.value: Turn today’s meetings into follow-ups. Find them with recall, then read_topic and read_source for the transcript itself; browse_index only if recall misses. Not search_files — it reads the assistant files folder, not the vault. Name an owner for an action item only where the transcript does.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_EveningWinddown_Query
data.value: Call query_todos with filter pending and query_reminders with filter active. Two short lists and nothing else: what went overdue today and is still open, then what is due or fires tomorrow. One line each with its time. No verdict on the day, no encouragement, no advice.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_HabitCheckin_Query
data.value: Call query_reminders and treat every reminder whose recurrence is not Once as a standing commitment, then call query_todos with filter completed. In at most three lines: which commitments were due today and whether anything matching them was ticked off. Then one question about the worst of them.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_BillsRenewals_Query
data.value: Call query_todos with filter all and query_reminders with filter all, then scan the titles, notes and descriptions for renewal, subscription, invoice, licence, insurance and membership wording. Report only what falls due in the next fourteen days, one line each, with its date and where you found it.

data.name: Routines_Blueprint_WeeklyReview_Query
data.value: Call query_todos with filter completed, then with filter all plus list_columns, then browse_index and read_topic. Four short sections: what was completed, what is open and past its due date, how the open items sit across the kanban columns, and two or three notes to carry into next week.

data.name: Settings_ExportDiagnostics_Description
data.value: Writes a redacted copy of Pia's own log files to a zip you can attach to a support request. Logs only — never chats, vault content, your history database or your provider credentials. File paths, your account and machine name, host names, e-mail addresses and tokens are replaced before anything is written, and every debug message body is dropped whole. The newest 7 log files up to 10 MB are included. Nothing is sent anywhere: the zip is written to your disk and you decide who sees it.

data.value: Pia is an AI system. Its answers, rewrites, summaries and spoken replies are generated by machine-learning models; the provider and model behind each answer are named beneath it, and exported files carry a machine-readable AI marking. Check important results before you rely on them.
